## Library Move Plan: Eight-Week Schedule (Weekend Volunteers & One Truck)

**Goal:** Successfully relocate the library collection to a new building within eight weeks, minimizing disruption to patrons and preserving the local history archive.

**Budget:** One rental truck.

**Assumptions:** Partially open library during weekdays (e.g., 9 AM - 5 PM), with reduced services during moving weeks. Volunteers available only on weekends.



---

**Phase 1: Planning & Preparation (Weeks 1-2)**

**Week 1: Logistics & Volunteer Onboarding**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Secure rental truck and insurance.
    *   Order packing supplies (boxes, tape, labels, bubble wrap, packing paper).  Prioritize eco-friendly packing materials where possible.
    *   Develop detailed labeling system (Category/Genre/Shelf Location).  Create a spreadsheet tracking all items.
    *   Recruit and onboard volunteers.  Develop a schedule and assign roles (packing, labeling, heavy lifting, archive handling). 
    *   **Archive:**  Secure a designated, climate-controlled area for the local history archive in the existing library (if available). Create a detailed inventory of archive items and assign a dedicated archival handling team.



**Week 2: Initial Packing & Baseline**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Begin packing Fiction (general fiction, large formats).  Label clearly (e.g., "Fiction - Mystery").  
    *   Start packing Audio Recordings (CDs/Cassettes) - categorize by genre (e.g., "Audio Dramas", "Classical Music"). Pad meticulously.
    *   Develop a clear unpacking plan for the new library – assigned areas for each section.
    *   **Volunteer Focus:** Training volunteers on safe lifting, proper packing techniques, labeling, and spreadsheet updates.




**Phase 2: High-Volume Packing & Archive Transition (Weeks 3-5)**

**Week 3:  Non-Fiction & Reference**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Pack Non-Fiction (History, Biography, Science, etc.). Label clearly (“Non-Fiction - History”).
    *   Begin packing Reference Materials (Dictionaries, Encyclopedias, Atlases). Handle with extra care.
    *   Inventory update on the spreadsheet.
    *   Continue archiving local history documents.

**Week 4:  Audio & Remaining Non-Fiction**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Continue packing Audio Recordings (remaining categories).
    *   Finish packing remaining Non-Fiction.
    *   Continue assigning archival items to the archiving team. Ensure proper environmental conditions.
    *   Evaluate packing progress – identify bottlenecks and adjust volunteer assignments.

**Week 5:  Big Print & Specials**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Pack Big Print books. Reinforce boxes due to size.
    *   Pack Special Collections (Rare books, manuscripts, maps - handled by archival team).  Ensure secure packaging.
    *   Confirm all inventory is accounted for in the spreadsheet. Begin reviewing the unpacking plan.

**Phase 3: Archive Relocation & Final Prep (Weeks 6-7)**

**Week 6: Archive Move & Truck Loading Prep**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Execute archive relocation to the new building with appropriate personnel and equipment. Coordinate with new staff.
    *   Begin loading the rental truck, starting with heavier items. Protect fragile items. 
    *   Continue packing Remaining Fiction. 
    *   Clean out areas of the old library as items are packed.

**Week 7:  Final Packing & Inventory Reconciliation**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Finish packing the remaining Fiction and Audio Recordings.
    *   Complete and verify the inventory spreadsheet. Address any discrepancies.
    *   Pack remaining Special Collections.
    *   Final walkthrough of the old library…ensure nothing is left behind.  Confirm all labeling is clear and accurate. 
    *   Organize a volunteer appreciation event.



**Phase 4: Truck Loading & Move Day (Weeks 8)**

**Week 8: Transport & Unpacking Begins**

*   **Tasks:**
    *   Load the rental truck. Ensure items are securely packed and protected during transport.
    *   Transport all packed items to the new library.
    *   Begin unpacking in the designated areas of the new library, following the pre-determined unpacking plan.
    *   **Post-Move:** Finalize shelving in the new library. Inspect collection for damage. Send thank-you notes to volunteers.



**Labeling & Sequencing Details:**

*   **Shelf Sections:**  Label boxes clearly with shelf sections (e.g., "Fiction A", "Fiction B", "Non-Fiction - History", "Audio - Biography").
*   **Genre within Category:** within each shelf section, further label boxes by genre (Mystery, Romance, Sci-Fi).
*  **Archive Specific Labeling**:  The archival items are meticulously labeled, not just for categorization but for specific provenance, date, and condition. 



**Volunteer Coordination:**

*   **Volunteer Coordinator:** Designate one person responsible for scheduling, communication, and volunteer onboarding.
*   **Weekly Briefings:** Hold brief weekly meetings to review progress, assign tasks, and address any issues.
*   **Team Rotation:** Rotate volunteer roles to ensure variety and prevent burnout.



**Important Considerations:**

*   **Patron Communication:**  Inform patrons about reduced library services during the move.  Provide updates on the relocation progress.

*   **Contingency Plan:** Allocate budget/time for unexpected issues.
*  **Packing Protocol:** Develop a document outlining packing procedures, preferred box sizes, and labeling standards
